evidence.text: Company guide math leaves room for a fourth straight raise or a narrowing up. FY2026 FFO As Adjusted is guided at $1.24-1.26, raised at Q1 (from $1.21-1.25) and again at Q2 (low end up from $1.22). H1 actual is $0.61, implying H2 of $0.63-0.65, while the Q3 consensus of $0.31 and the FY consensus of $1.24 sit at or below the bottom of that implied path. Management said same-property NOI is tracking above the midpoint of its 5-9% range after 8.7% in Q2, and the signed-not-open pipeline is a record $16.5m (about $0.01 of FFO in H2 2026). Against this, management flagged about a penny of drag from investment-management sales before redeployment, which is already inside the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market believed the midpoint or top of the guide, FY consensus would sit at $1.25 or above rather than $1.24, and the stock would not be down about 17% since a print that raised guidance. The EW preview explicitly reads the bottom-of-range consensus as Street doubt about the upper half.

evidence.text: Q3 2026 was the hottest US summer on record, and every month of the quarter set a national record: July 2026 was the warmest month on record for the contiguous US, August the warmest August, and September the warmest September. Texas had triple-digit record highs on 2026-08-22, and Extreme Heat Warnings covered NW Louisiana, E Texas and S Arkansas. ERCOT set an all-time peak of 91.1 GW and SPP 58.0 GW; MISO reached 121.5 GW, within 4% of its record. Against this, Entergy's Q3 2025 weather contribution was only +$0.06/share. Read across that weather gap, a Q3 EPS print of perhaps $0.05-0.12 above the ~$1.72 bar is plausible, and FY2026 could move toward the top of the $4.25-4.45 guide. YTD weather through H1 2026 was -$0.02.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 printed $1.53 with +$0.06 of weather and a narrowed guide, and the stock moved +0.46%. evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus has risen only from $1.67 (AAII, August) to about $1.70-1.73, which is +11-13% YoY. That is consistent with rate actions plus normal weather, not with a record-heat quarter. Had the market fully priced the heat, Q3 estimates would sit well above $1.75 and the FY consensus above $4.40. Still, the weather is public and analysts partly adjust for it, so this is at best partly unpriced.

evidence.text: At Q3 2025 Entergy both narrowed its FY guidance and extended its multi-year outlook. If the market had fully priced an above-plan political quarter, the stock would not have fallen 5.4% in the five days before the print. FNC ad revenue sits in the Cable segment, which already showed EBITDA -3% in Q4 FY26 on World Cup rights amortisation. Lower demo delivery means more audience-deficiency units and less scatter pricing in Jul-Sep.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: FNC ratings are not broken out in the release. FOX News Media's record revenue in FY26 (2026-08-06 call: +400 advertisers) was part of the beat bought +5.3%. No prior print found where an FNC ratings decline was the stated cause of a move.
evidence.why_not_priced: The ratings are public, and analysts know a slow news quarter follows a heavy one. But the preview coverage found (Earnings Whispers 10-26) lists Tubi, political, the World Cup tail and digital losses as the swing factors and does not mention FNC audience erosion. If it were priced, the preview risk list would name cable news ad softness, and the skew would not be call-bid. Net of the rest of the company: FNC advertising is perhaps a tenth of quarterly revenue, while TV-segment political and World Cup revenue sit far above it. So this trims the beat rather than reversing it.
evidence.independence: Adweek TVNewser Q3 2026 ratings (https://www.adweek.com/tvnewser/here-are-the-3rd-quarter-of-2026-cable-news-ratings/) carries the same Nielsen data, so it is the same underlying source. evidence.text: FOX One retention after its World Cup surge is better than at launch. Antenna counts 2.8M gross sign-ups in June 2026, 93% new to the service (2026-07-22). YipitData (2026-08-21) finds 43.1% of the June cohort had a captured cancellation within 60 days, against 52.4% for the Aug-Oct 2025 launch cohort. That points to a larger retained base feeding distribution revenue in Jul-Sep, consistent with management's 'retention surpassed expectations'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q4 FY26, distribution +5% with FOX One 'exceeding expectations' was part of a print bought +5.3%. FOX One is not separately disclosed in revenue.
evidence.why_not_priced: Panel data is not in consensus models, and Fox does not disclose subscribers. But a 43% 60-day churn still means a large share of the June cohort left before the NFL season, and both figures are floors (silent cancels). The finding is small and could go either way relative to the sell-side's assumed retention.
evidence.independence: Antenna June sign-ups (https://www.newscaststudio.com/2026/07/22/fifa-world-cup-drove-2-8m-fox-one-sign-ups-in-june/) is a different panel but measures acquisition, not retention.

evidence.text: The company's own last word on this quarter was unusually firm. On the 2026-08-06 call Murdoch said 'Fiscal 2027 is also off to an excellent start', with continued ad momentum across national, local and digital in FQ1, and 'one of the strongest upfronts in our history, with double-digit growth in volume'. evidence.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: it is the reason consensus sits at +13-15% revenue and the whisper above consensus. It is filed because it is the company-level primary statement that the quarter lands inside, and because a company that said 'excellent start' five weeks into the quarter has a track record (8 of 8 beats).
